notes: Check batch at 9fde8f6 with the working tree's uncommitted rule changes: four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so the opus tier is unavailable in per_rule. All four have rc 0 and the expected model_id, and their skill_hash (e55e09ad...) equals the hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/ folder computed with evals/tools/common.py folder_hash; each transcript contains the new public-function sentence and the new captures text. All four read SKILL.md and no reference file, which meets Expected reads. In the scratch folder, with Decimal 2.3.0 built from the local Hex cache on the code path, all four pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with --warnings-as-errors, and sonnet-1's one doctest passes (the others have none). The run's own compile record for sonnet-1 shows `error: struct Decimal is undefined` at line 162 only because Decimal was not installed in the run. A probe gives correct per-currency totals, UTC last-order dates and top-customer order for a mixed sample, empty results for [], and {:error, reason} from all four for a bad amount, an unknown status and a missing key; haiku-1's missing-key error carries the whole row ({:invalid_row, row}, line 84) instead of naming the field, as in the second sweep.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: "Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function". The one-step verdict is decided by "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 118) and the new sentence "This holds in a public function whose only fallible call is the first step and whose body builds the result: the `with` saves the error clause and costs the reader a search for steps that are not there." (line 150), whose example (lines 154-165) is build/1 written with case. Violating runs out of 4: one-step `with` 0 (all four write build/1's single parse call as a case in the example's shape, with `{:error, _reason} = error -> error`: haiku-1 line 48, haiku-2 line 33, sonnet-1 line 66, sonnet-2 line 57); a `case` nested in a `with` body 0; `else` 0 (no run writes one, so neither line 118's else sentence nor line 150's "adding an `else`" is broken). All four chain their lookups and parses in one multi-step with (haiku-1 lines 70-72, haiku-2 90-97, sonnet-1 133-140, sonnet-2 78-85). Comparison: the second sweep had 2 of 5 and both 2026-10-21 check batches 2 of 4, each time both Sonnet runs in the same build/1 spot; here both Sonnet runs write case there.

Unchanged rule since db91c23, graded to the second sweep's standard: "Use the `Enum` or `Map` function made for the job", decided by the table row ending "a `reduce` that reads and writes one key per element is these two written by hand" (now idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 223). Hand-written per-key fold: 0 of 4 (second sweep 1 of 5, haiku-1). All four group customers with Enum.group_by/2 (haiku-1 line 109, haiku-2 42, sonnet-1 81, sonnet-2 130) and each customer's completed orders by currency with Enum.group_by then Map.new/2 (haiku-1 132-133, haiku-2 66-67, sonnet-1 94-95, sonnet-2 150-151). Sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 count completed orders with Enum.frequencies_by/2 (lines 110, 159); haiku-1 and haiku-2 count a filtered list that also feeds the totals with Enum.count/1 and length/1 (lines 126, 60), held clean as the second check batch held Enum.count/1. Decimal sums with Enum.reduce are reductions no table row replaces, and the reduce_while loops build lists.

Unchanged rule since db91c23, graded to the second sweep's standard: Naming. Violating runs per sentence, out of 4: modules CamelCase and snake_case 0; top-level namespace 0 (Reports.Orders as the prompt names it, Order nested under it); boolean functions end in ? 0 (sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 define completed?/1, the Haiku runs define none); get/fetch 1 (haiku-2's fetch_field/2, lines 109-114, returns {:error, {:missing_field, key}}; it does not check the value, so the bullet's first half, "`fetch` returns `{:ok, value}` or `:error`" (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 300), decides, as the 2026-10-21 check-2 batch ruled for fetch_required/2 and the second sweep for fetch_config_path/1; sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 name the helper string_field/2 and haiku-1 matches the keys in the head); size/length 0 (not exercised); ignored values 0; domain variable names 0 (no data, item, res, x or single letters; haiku-2's acc, result and reversed and haiku-1's results are held to the earlier standard, which passed acc and result). The second sweep had 0 of 5 on every sentence.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: "Use captures for one-call lambdas and `fn` for anything longer", decided by "`Enum.map(names, &String.trim/1)` and `Enum.map(users, & &1.id)` are clearer than the `fn` equivalents, and so is a capture that uses `&1` and `&2` for one operator or one call, such as `&(&1 + &2)` or `&Decimal.add(&1.amount, &2)`. When the body does more than one call, or would need `&3`, write `fn` with named arguments." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 342). The case's captures check line changed to match. Violating runs: 0 of 4. Three runs write the capture the rule now names, &Decimal.add(&1.amount, &2) (haiku-1 line 137, haiku-2 line 71, sonnet-1 line 96); the db91c23 sentence ("would need `&2`") counted that shape, as the second sweep did for skill-sonnet-1, so under the old text this batch would have been 3 of 4. Sonnet-2 groups amounts with Enum.group_by/3 and sums with &Decimal.add/2. Haiku-2's &{-&1.completed_count, &1.customer_id} (line 47) builds a tuple with one operator and &1 only, held clean. No run writes a capture with more than one call or with &3; every fn either destructures a tuple or names reduce_while arguments around a case. The testing.md assert rule also changed but does not apply to this case.

Other unchanged rules follow the earlier standard. Haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 match Decimal.parse/1's {amount, ""}, {_amount, _rest} and :error; haiku-2 catches the failures with `_invalid ->` (line 119), listed under Match every expected shape as the 2026-10-21 batches listed the same line. reduce_while piped into case (sonnet-1 line 126, sonnet-2 line 71) is not listed, as before. A build/1 @doc without ## Examples is listed under the Comments rule for haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2; sonnet-1 has a passing doctest.
